## Yes — the repo ships zero agent-facing context

`crimes scan --format json` surfaces exactly one finding for this, and it's unambiguous:

```json
{
  "id": "crime_00018",
  "type": "missing_agent_context",
  "charge": "Missing Agent Context",
  "severity": "medium",
  "confidence": 0.9,
  "scores": { "agent_risk": 0.53 }
}
```

Its evidence enumerates all four surfaces the detector checks, and all four are absent:

- no `AGENTS.md` at repo root
- no `CLAUDE.md` at repo root
- no `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`
- no `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md`
- `package.json` declares bin(s): `tsup`, `tsup-node` — agents have no way to discover commands

Note what this is *not* saying: the repo isn't undocumented. `docs/README.md` is 679 lines (it's its own finding, `crime_00006`, "God File"). That's user-facing prose about how to *use* tsup — not instructions on how to *change* it. The detector is measuring a different thing: is there a file an agent loads before its first edit.

## Why this matters for your first PR specifically

Missing context isn't dangerous alone — it's dangerous in combination with the rest of this scan, and this repo has the bad combination:

**1. No conventions to read → agent infers them from code that's already drifting.** The scan flags `boolean_naming_drift` in four files (`silent`, `inline`, `clearCache`, `enabled`), `option_bag_junk_drawer` in four functions, and `return_shape_roulette` in three. An agent with no AGENTS.md will pattern-match on the existing code and reproduce the drift, because from the inside it looks like the house style.

**2. No "load-bearing" warnings → agent refactors the wrong file first.** `src/utils.ts` has fan-in 18, `src/plugin.ts` fan-in 10, `src/log.ts` fan-in 9 — and `src/utils.ts` is also a 425-line God File with 7 sync I/O calls. Every signal says "clean me up." Nothing in the repo says "29 modules ride on this." A first-PR agent doing a good-faith tidy in `utils.ts` has a blast radius it can't see.

**3. Weak tests won't catch the mistake.** This is the part that makes it bite. There are 16 `weak_test_signal` findings — 12 tests with **zero** `expect`/`assert` calls (`test/example.test.ts`, `test/graphql.test.ts`, `test/shims.test.ts`, `test/tsconfig.test.ts`, several in `test/experimental-dts.test.ts`) plus 12 more that only use weak matchers. So the normal safety net — "make the change, run the tests, trust green" — is partly theatre here. An agent with no context makes a confident wrong edit, the suite goes green, and the PR looks clean.

The chain is: no instructions → wrong assumption → no assertion to contradict it → merged. That's why `missing_agent_context` carries `agent_risk` 0.53 despite only medium severity — the aggregate risk is about what it *lets through*, not the file itself.

## Minimal AGENTS.md that clears the finding

The detector is satisfied by an `AGENTS.md` at repo root. Keeping it minimal is the right call — a short file that's true beats a long one that rots. Everything below is anchored to what the scan actually observed about this repo.

```markdown
# AGENTS.md

Instructions for coding agents working in this repo. Read before editing.

## What this is

`tsup` — a TypeScript/JS bundler. Ships two binaries: `tsup` and `tsup-node`.
Users depend on our output format staying stable; treat CLI flags and emitted
file layout as public API.

## Commands

- Install: `pnpm install`
- Build: `pnpm build`
- Test: `pnpm test`
- Typecheck: `pnpm typecheck`
- Lint: `pnpm lint`

Run build + test before proposing any change.

## Layout

- `src/index.ts` — main `build()` entry and option normalization
- `src/cli-main.ts` — CLI arg parsing; delegates to `build()`
- `src/esbuild/` — esbuild pipeline and plugins (postcss, svelte, swc)
- `src/rollup.ts`, `src/rollup/` — the .d.ts rollup path
- `src/plugin.ts` — plugin container; the hook contract lives here
- `src/utils.ts`, `src/log.ts` — shared helpers
- `test/` — integration tests; most build a fixture and inspect output

## Load-bearing files — prefer additive changes

These have wide fan-in. Restructuring them ripples across the repo:

- `src/utils.ts` (18 importers)
- `src/plugin.ts` (10 importers) — also the plugin hook contract
- `src/log.ts` (9 importers)
- `test/utils.ts` (9 importers) — changing its helpers can silently
  weaken many tests at once

If a change here seems necessary, say so in the PR description rather
than folding it into unrelated work.

## Conventions

- Booleans are prefixed `is` / `has` / `should` / `can`. Existing names
  like `silent`, `inline`, `clearCache`, `enabled` predate this — don't
  copy them into new code.
- Functions returning more than one object shape need an explicit return
  type or a discriminated union.
- Prefer async I/O in `src/`. `*Sync` calls are legacy, not the pattern.
- `Options` is the user-facing config type. New internal state gets its
  own named type; don't widen the options bag.

## Testing

Every test must assert observable behaviour — file contents, emitted
output, thrown errors. A test that only runs a build and finishes is
not a test. Some existing tests in `test/` do exactly that; they are
known gaps, not a template.

## Don't

- Don't change emitted output shape or CLI flag names without flagging it.
- Don't add a new bundler or transform dependency without discussion.
- Don't reformat files you aren't otherwise touching.
```

That's roughly 60 lines. It clears `crime_00018` on the next scan, and — more usefully — the "Load-bearing files" and "Testing" sections are the two that would have actually stopped the failure mode above.

**One judgment call worth flagging:** I filled the Commands section with conventional pnpm scripts. The scan tells us the binaries are `tsup` and `tsup-node` but doesn't expose `package.json`'s `scripts` block, so verify those five commands against the real file before committing — a wrong command in AGENTS.md is worse than no AGENTS.md, since agents will run it confidently. Everything else in the skeleton is derived directly from findings in the scan.
